detail.longDescription: I'm working on some S3 buckets with quantities of data up to 200TB. The data is most likely text logs or images, all quite small objects. I want to review this data programmatically to decide what I can trim away or move to deep storage. Should a directory have very few images in, or only be small, I might trim it; should it hold masses of files I'll likely archive it. Notably the location within a directory structure may be taken into account too. My concern is that the cost of even just running aws s3 ls --recursive on one of these buckets could get quite expensive quite quickly. What's the cheapest method to review all this with? At the moment my running theory is that I could have a program that runs recursive ls from root once and then parses the result into a locally stored model of directories and file sizes which I could then navigate and query. However, this feels like a lot of work and I'm surprised this isn't an issue other people have come across, is there a simple solution that I'm missing?
